entries.paragraph_1: Sen. Dan Sullivan’s (R-AK) defeat to Rep.-elect Mary Peltola (D-AK) in Alaska was more than another casualty in a disastrous midterm cycle . entries.paragraph_2: Heading into November, the Trump administration tried to rescue Sullivan and replicate its 2024 pitch across the Rust Belt, through classic top-down industrial policy. entries.title: Lee Nak-yeon and Abe agree S. Korea-Japan relations cannot remain in current state
entries.paragraph_1: South Korean Prime Minister Lee Nak-yeon and Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe reached an agreement in a meeting on Oct. 24 that bilateral relations cannot be left in their current strained state. While the two sides did not succeed in bridging their differences over a South Korean Supreme Court ruling ordering compensation for forced labor mobilization during the Japanese occupation of Korea, analysts said they potentially paved the way for restoring senior-level dialogue to reverse the spiral in their relations.
entries.paragraph_2: Lee met with Abe for 21 minutes at the Japanese Prime Minister’s residence in Tokyo’s Chiyoda Ward on the morning of Oct. 24 while visiting Japan to attend its imperial enthronement. The originally scheduled meeting time was around 10 minutes, but the two ended up talking for longer, with Lee delivering a letter to Abe from South Korean President Moon Jae-in. After the meeting, First Vice Foreign Minister Cho Se-young explained, “With regard to South Korea-Japan relations, both prime ministers agreed that the two countries are important neighbors that cannot afford to leave relations in their current difficult state, and they also agreed that non-governmental interchange, including interchange among young people from both countries, is all the more important when the situation is difficult.”

entries.title: South Korea's $1 Trillion Export Phenomenon | Armstrong Economics
entries.paragraph_1: South Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports, becoming only the fourth country in history to reach that milestone, joining the United States, Germany, and China. This is a country that emerged from the Korean War devastated, impoverished, and dependent upon foreign assistance. In the 1960s, Koreans were exporting wigs made from human hair, squid, pig bristles, and whatever else they could sell to earn foreign currency. Today, they are producing the semiconductors powering the global artificial intelligence revolution. This is what happens when a nation develops its productive economy instead of expecting government spending to manufacture prosperity.
entries.paragraph_2: Korean exports have increased more than 36,000-fold since 1948. As recently as 1964, annual exports were only $100 million. They crossed $1 trillion on November 19, 2026, and are projected to reach $1.17 trillion by year-end. The transformation did not happen overnight. South Korea developed steelmaking, shipbuilding, automobiles, electronics, and eventually advanced semiconductors. Its companies invested in manufacturing capabilities that could compete internationally. Samsung, Hyundai, and SK hynix became global industrial powers because they produced goods that consumers and businesses around the world wanted to purchase.

North Gyeongsang Province mistakenly described the aircraft as suspected North Korean planes using an outdated drill template. South Korea plans to summon a Russian diplomat to lodge a formal protest. The incident follows multiple recent Russian entries into the zone amid heightened Korean Peninsula tensions. AIR RAID evacuation warning turns out to be false alarm When the Interior Ministry's text message hit phones at 7:52 a.m. commanding "EVACUATION, AIR RAID," residents of Ulleung Island had every reason to believe the worst. This is a community still haunted by November 2022 when a North Korean missile screaming toward their island triggered real sirens and civilians scattered with no clue where to seek refuge. But this time the threat was not a missile but a flight of Russian aircraft that never violated South Korean airspace, only its monitoring zone. An air defense identification zone is not sovereign territory but a buffer where a country tracks approaching planes. Russian military aircraft have repeatedly tested this boundary, entering the zone on Nov. 17, Aug. 25 and June 27 of this year alone, according to Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff. Moscow has long rejected the legal basis of South Korea's identification zone and routinely fails to notify Seoul before entering, a practice that turns every approach into a guessing game that ordinary civilians pay for with their peace of mind. The South Korean Air Force scrambled F-15K fighters after detecting the Russian aircraft and conducted tactical maneuvers to prepare for contingencies. A JCS official said the planes flew close to South Korean airspace but moved away toward the East Sea after the military response. The Interior Ministry lifted the alert about three minutes later after the aircraft left the area. Yet those three minutes were enough to expose a deeper dysfunction. The English version of the initial alert read "EVACUATION, AIR RAID," a level far above the precautionary alert the military intended. SBS News reported that the ministry's message erroneously described a flight object presumed to be Russian as having violated airspace, directly contradicting the military's assessment. At 7:58 a.m., North Gyeongsang Province sent its own cancellation message stating the alert was lifted "because an object presumed to be a North Korean aircraft had left the danger zone." The JoongAng Daily captured the absurdity with its headline questioning whether the aircraft were Russian or North Korean. Provincial officials later admitted they had used an outdated emergency drill template created for a North Korean aircraft scenario. It took approximately 40 minutes before the message was corrected to identify the aircraft as Russian. For the residents of Ulleung Island, who lived through real missile alerts and knew firsthand the terror of not knowing where to run, this bureaucratic theater was worse than incompetence. It was a betrayal of trust. The diplomatic response followed a script as predictable as the provocation itself. South Korea's Defense Ministry announced it would summon a Russian diplomat from the Russian Embassy in Seoul to lodge a formal protest, according to Yonhap News Agency. Yet Russia does not even recognize the legal basis of South Korea's identification zone and has stated clearly that Seoul's claimed control over it lacks foundation in international law. This diplomatic ritual of summoning an ambassador who will reject the protest's premise while the aircraft keep coming has become a meaningless dance. Under standard international practice, military aircraft entering another country's zone submit a flight plan in advance and report their position upon entry. Russia refuses to follow this protocol, and Seoul has no mechanism to compel compliance. The Russian warplanes did not fire a single shot, but they accomplished something far more insidious. They demonstrated that South Korea's defense establishment cannot distinguish a routine incursion from an invasion, cannot issue a clear warning, and cannot even correctly identify which country's aircraft is approaching its shores. entries.paragraph_1: Today’s trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin might be as significant as the Yalta Conference in 1945, in which the three great Allies carved up the world map after the Second World War. entries.paragraph_2: The context of economic discussion is what lubricates this particular ménage à trois. Xi is not hosting his counterparts in Beijing – a setting that would lend a political overtone – but in Shenzhen . This week, China’s tech hub is dazzling crowds with laser-light shows and more than 100 Fortune 500 CEOs have flown into the city. Interestingly, the roster for the summit comprises “member economies” rather than states, so Hong Kong and Taiwan are able to participate. But the frenzy will reach a crescendo today as the leaders of China, Russia and the US retreat from the city to the Qilin Mountain Villa: a location that feels markedly different from San Francisco, Lima and Busan, which hosted the past three bilateral Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summits with Xi.

entries.title: South Korean president calls for renewed talks with North Korea, lasting peace
entries.paragraph_1: Beijing, Nov. 19 (SANA) South Korean President Lee Jae-Myung on Thursday called for renewed dialogue with North Korea to formally end the decades-long conflict on the Korean Peninsula , saying lasting peace was essential to stability and prosperity across the Asia-Pacific region.
entries.paragraph_2: Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC ) summit in Shenzhen, China, Lee expressed hope that talks with Pyongyang could resume and lead to a permanent peace arrangement, according to Yonhap News Agency. “We hope that the door to dialogue with North Korea will reopen, leading to discussions on ending the long-standing war on the Korean Peninsula and establishing a permanent peace regime,” Lee said. He reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to achieving lasting peace on the peninsula and urged regional countries to support diplomatic efforts toward that goal. Addressing economic challenges, Lee warned that disruptions to the global trading system and mounting uncertainty required closer cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies . He said recent geopolitical crises had highlighted the region’s economic interdependence, with disruptions in one country capable of rapidly affecting neighboring economies. Lee called for stronger protection of the multilateral trading system and greater regional cooperation to stabilize supply chains and strengthen economic resilience. His remarks come as South Korea and the United States seek to revive diplomatic engagement with North Korea amid continuing tensions over Pyongyang’s nuclear program. Speculation has also grown over a possible meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on the sidelines of the APEC summit, although a South Korean presidential official said such a meeting remained uncertain. The Korean War, fought from 1950 to 1953, ended in an armistice rather than a formal peace treaty, leaving the two Koreas technically at war.

entries.paragraph_1: નવી દિલ્હી : આંતરરાષ્ટ્રીય સ્તરે તણાવભરી પરિસ્થિતિ વચ્ચે સાઉથ કોરિયા માં એક એવી સનસનાટીભરી ઘટના બની છે , જેણે ક્ષણભરમાં યુદ્ધ જેવો માહોલ સર્જી દીધો હતો . રશિયાના વિમાનો દેખાતા સાઉથ કોરિયાએ તાત્કાલિક પોતાના ફાઈટર જેટ્સ આકાશમાં ઉડાવ્યા હતા અને સાવચેતીના ભાગરૂપે ટાપુ ખાલી કરવાનું એલર્ટ જારી કર્યું હતું , પરંતુ માત્ર ૩ મિનિટ બાદ આ એલર્ટ પાછું ખેંચી લેવામાં આવતા ભારે હડકંપ અને ચકચાર મચી ગઈ છે . એર ડિફેન્સ આઇડેન્ટિફિકેશન ઝોન એ કોઈપણ દેશ દ્વારા પોતાની હવાઈ સીમાની સુરક્ષા માટે નક્કી કરવામાં આવેલો એક ખાસ વિસ્તાર છે . આ ઝોનની મદદથી દેશની હવાઈ સીમા તરફ આવી રહેલા કોઈપણ અજાણ્યા કે વિદેશી વિમાનની સમયસર ઓળખ કરી શકાય છે અને જરૂર પડ્યે તાત્કાલિક જવાબી કાર્યવાહી કરી શકાય છે . આ ઘટના પહેલા સાઉથ કોરિયાના સુરક્ષા મંત્રાલયે પૂર્વ કિનારે આવેલા ઉલેઉંગ ટાપુ (Ulleung island) માટે ખાલી કરવાની ચેતવણી ( ઇવેક્યુએશન વોર્નિંગ ) જાહેર કરી હતી . મંત્રાલયે તે સમયે કહ્યું હતું કે એક રશિયન વિમાન દેશની હવાઈ સીમામાં પ્રવેશ્યું છે . જોકે , માત્ર ત્રણ મિનિટ બાદ આ ચેતવણી પાછી ખેંચી લેવામાં આવી હતી . સ્થાનિક ન્યૂઝ એજન્સી ' યોનહાપ ' ના અહેવાલ મુજબ , સ્થાનિક પ્રશાસન દ્વારા ભૂલથી ઉલેઉંગ વિસ્તાર નજીક ઉત્તર કોરિયાનું વિમાન હોવાની ચેતવણી પણ થોડીવાર માટે જાહેર થઈ ગઈ હતી , જેને બાદમાં રદ કરવામાં આવી હતી .
